\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Depth3 Switching}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.Depth3Switching
\section{Overview}

This module formalizes the switching argument for depth-3 circuits in normal form: a
depth-3 AND-of-OR-of-AND circuit is written as the AND of $s_2$ width-$w$ DNF gates.
It provides the one-step depth-3 to depth-2 compression, the two-stage switching bound
under a composed random restriction, and the resulting circuit-reduction probability
bounds, together with the CNF-cleaning machinery (tautology removal and per-clause
variable deduplication) needed to put restricted gates into normal form.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction by a composite equals iterated restriction]
\lean{LMN.restrictFn_composeRestr}
\label{LMN.restrictFn_composeRestr}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.extend, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$ be a Boolean function on $n$
variables, and let $\rho_1, \rho_2 : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{0, 1, *\}$ be two
restrictions, where a coordinate is either fixed to a Boolean value or left free. Write
$\rho_1 * \rho_2$ for their composition, the restriction that on each coordinate takes
the value fixed by $\rho_1$ if there is one and otherwise the value assigned by
$\rho_2$, and for a restriction $\rho$ write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function $x
\mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ obtained by evaluating $f$ with the fixed
coordinates of $\rho$ substituted and the free coordinates read off from $x$. Then
restricting $f$ by the composite restriction agrees with restricting first by $\rho_1$
and then by $\rho_2$:
\[
f\!\restriction_{\rho_1 * \rho_2} \;=\;
\bigl(f\!\restriction_{\rho_1}\bigr)\!\restriction_{\rho_2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Decision-tree depth respects pointwise equality]
\lean{LMN.dtDepth_congr}
\label{LMN.dtDepth_congr}
\leanok
\uses{dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f$ and $g$ be Boolean functions of $n$ variables, that is, maps $\{0,1\}^n \to
\{0,1\}$, and suppose they agree on every input, so $f(x) = g(x)$ for all $x \in
\{0,1\}^n$. Then $f$ and $g$ have the same decision-tree depth.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restriction respects pointwise equality]
\lean{LMN.restrictFn_congr}
\label{LMN.restrictFn_congr}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f, g : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2\text{-valued Boolean inputs}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$
be two Boolean functions on $n$ variables that agree everywhere, $f(y) = g(y)$ for every
input $y$, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables. Then the restricted
functions agree as well: writing $f_\rho(x) = f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ for the
restriction of $f$ by $\rho$, one has $f_\rho(x) = g_\rho(x)$ for every $x :
\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Pointwise AND of a list of functions]
\lean{LMN.listAnd}
\label{LMN.listAnd}
\leanok
The pointwise conjunction of a list of Boolean functions: the empty list yields the
constant $\mathrm{true}$ function, and $f :: fs$ evaluates at $x$ to $f(x)$ AND the
value of the list $fs$ at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Restriction commutes with list conjunction]
\lean{LMN.restrictFn_listAnd}
\label{LMN.restrictFn_listAnd}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.listAnd, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f_1, \dots, f_k$ be Boolean functions on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a
restriction of those variables, and write $f|_\rho$ for the restriction of a function
$f$ along $\rho$ (the function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$). Then restricting
the pointwise conjunction $f_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge f_k$ along $\rho$ agrees, at every
point $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$, with the pointwise conjunction of the
individually restricted functions $f_1|_\rho, \dots, f_k|_\rho$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[One-step depth-3 compression under a random restriction]
\lean{LMN.depth3_compression}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b004
}
\label{LMN.depth3_compression}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.compression_and_of_cnfs, LMN.listAnd, LMN.one_step_reduction_with_compression, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{6}
Fix $n \ge 1$, and let $D_1,\dots,D_{s_2}$ be DNF formulas on $n$ variables, each of
width at most $w$ with $w \ge 1$, subject to the two syntactic conditions that within
every term any two literals on the same variable coincide (so no term repeats a variable
with opposite polarities) and that no term lists the same literal twice. Let $l \in
\bbn$, and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le 1/(40w)$ and $p \le 1$. Draw a
Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables. Then with probability at
least
\[
1 - s_2\!\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} +
\exp\!\left(-\,\tfrac{np}{3}\right)\right)
\]
there exists a CNF formula $\Psi$ of width at most $l$ that computes the conjunction of
the restricted gates: writing $D_i\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function $x \mapsto
D_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ obtained by fixing the coordinates set by $\rho$ and
leaving the free coordinates to $x$, one has $\Psi(x) = \bigwedge_{i=1}^{s_2}
\bigl(D_i\!\restriction_\rho\bigr)(x)$ for every assignment $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tautological clause]
\lean{LMN.clauseIsTaut}
\label{LMN.clauseIsTaut}
\leanok
\uses{Literal}
A clause (a list of literals interpreted as their disjunction) is tautological if it
contains two literals on the same variable with opposite signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Tautological clauses are satisfied by every assignment]
\lean{LMN.clauseIsTaut_eval_true}
\label{LMN.clauseIsTaut_eval_true}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.clauseIsTaut, Literal, Literal.eval}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ be a clause on the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$, that is, a list of literals
read as their disjunction, where a literal is a variable together with a sign and
evaluates to that variable's value if positive and to its negation if negated. Suppose
$c$ is tautological: it contains two literals on the same variable with opposite signs.
Then for every Boolean assignment $x \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to
\{\text{true},\text{false}\}$, at least one literal of $c$ evaluates to $\mathrm{true}$,
so the disjunction of the literals of $c$ evaluates to $\mathrm{true}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Deduplicate clause variables]
\lean{LMN.dedupClauseVars}
\label{LMN.dedupClauseVars}
\leanok
\uses{Literal}
Removes duplicate variables from a clause, keeping the first occurrence of each
variable.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Variable-injectivity of a deduplicated clause]
\lean{LMN.dedupClauseVars_var_inj}
\label{LMN.dedupClauseVars_var_inj}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.dedupClauseVars, Literal}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ be a clause, that is, a list of literals over the variables $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$,
each literal consisting of a variable together with a negation flag. Form the
deduplicated clause obtained from $c$ by keeping, for each variable, only its first
occurrence. Then any two literals of this deduplicated clause that share the same
variable are in fact the same literal; equivalently, distinct literals of the
deduplicated clause have distinct variables.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Deduplicated clause has no repeated literals]
\lean{LMN.dedupClauseVars_nodup}
\label{LMN.dedupClauseVars_nodup}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.dedupClauseVars, Literal}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a finite list of literals over the variable set $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, and form
a new list from $c$ by scanning left to right and discarding every literal whose
variable has already appeared, keeping only the first occurrence of each variable. Then
this deduplicated list is repetition-free: no literal occurs in it more than once.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Deduplication does not increase clause length]
\lean{LMN.dedupClauseVars_length_le}
\label{LMN.dedupClauseVars_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.dedupClauseVars, Literal}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a clause, that is, a finite list of literals over the variables
$\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, and let $\mathrm{dedup}(c)$ be the clause obtained from $c$ by
retaining, for each variable, only its first occurring literal and discarding every
later literal on the same variable. Then the length of $\mathrm{dedup}(c)$ is at most
the length of $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Deduplication preserves evaluation of non-tautological clauses]
\lean{LMN.dedupClauseVars_eval_of_not_taut}
\label{LMN.dedupClauseVars_eval_of_not_taut}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.clauseIsTaut, LMN.dedupClauseVars, Literal, Literal.eval}
Let $c$ be a clause over the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$ — a list of literals read as
their disjunction, where a literal evaluates to $x_i$ if positive and $\lnot x_i$ if
negated. Suppose $c$ is not tautological, meaning it contains no two literals on the
same variable with opposite signs. Then for every Boolean assignment $x \colon
\{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, the clause obtained from $c$ by
keeping only the first literal on each variable evaluates to the same truth value as $c$
itself.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Clean a CNF]
\lean{LMN.cleanCNF_D3}
\label{LMN.cleanCNF_D3}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, LMN.clauseIsTaut, LMN.dedupClauseVars}
Cleans a CNF by removing all tautological clauses and then deduplicating the variables
within each remaining clause.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Cleaning preserves CNF evaluation]
\lean{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_eval}
\label{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_eval}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.evalClause, LMN.clauseIsTaut, LMN.clauseIsTaut_eval_true, LMN.cleanCNF_D3}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula over $n$ Boolean variables — a conjunction of clauses, each
clause a disjunction of literals — and let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ be an assignment. Form the
cleaned formula from $\psi$ by first deleting every tautological clause (a clause
containing two literals on the same variable with opposite signs) and then, within each
surviving clause, keeping only the first literal on each variable and discarding later
literals on variables already seen. Then the cleaned formula and $\psi$ evaluate to the
same Boolean value on $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cleaning a CNF does not increase its width]
\lean{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_width_le}
\label{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_width_le}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.width, LMN.cleanCNF_D3, LMN.dedupClauseVars_length_le, Term, Term.width}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula over $n$ variables, and form its cleaned version by
discarding every tautological clause (one containing two literals on the same variable
with opposite signs) and then, within each surviving clause, keeping only the first
occurrence of each variable. Writing the width of a CNF formula for the largest number
of literals in any of its clauses (and $0$ for the empty formula), the width of the
cleaned formula is at most the width of $\psi$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cleaned clauses have no repeated literals]
\lean{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_nodup}
\label{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_nodup}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, LMN.cleanCNF_D3, LMN.dedupClauseVars_nodup}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula over $n$ variables, and let $\mathrm{clean}(\psi)$ be the
formula obtained from $\psi$ by discarding every tautological clause and then, in each
surviving clause, keeping only the first literal on each variable. Then every clause of
$\mathrm{clean}(\psi)$, viewed as a list of literals, contains no repeated literal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Variable-injective clauses in a cleaned CNF]
\lean{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_var_inj}
\label{LMN.cleanCNF_D3_var_inj}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, LMN.cleanCNF_D3, LMN.dedupClauseVars, LMN.dedupClauseVars_var_inj}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula over the variables $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. After cleaning $\psi$
— that is, after discarding every tautological clause and then deduplicating the
variables within each surviving clause — every clause becomes variable-injective: in any
clause of the cleaned formula, any two literals sharing the same variable are in fact
the same literal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction of a CNF to a duplicate-free normal form]
\lean{LMN.exists_nice_cnf_of_cnf}
\label{LMN.exists_nice_cnf_of_cnf}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, LMN.cleanCNF_D3, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_eval, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_nodup, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_var_inj, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_width_le}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula in the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$, written as a conjunction
of clauses, each clause a disjunction of literals. Then there is a CNF formula $\psi'$
that computes the same Boolean function as $\psi$, that is, $\psi'(x)=\psi(x)$ for every
assignment $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, whose width (the maximum number of literals in any of its
clauses) is at most that of $\psi$, and in which every clause is free of repetition in
the strong sense that no literal occurs twice and no two distinct literals share a
variable.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{2}
Let $f\colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n$
variables, and let $d$ be a natural number. If the decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most
$d$, then there is a CNF formula $\psi$ that computes $f$ (that is, $\psi(x) = f(x)$ for
every assignment $x$) and whose width is at most $d$, meaning every clause has at most
$d$ literals. Moreover $\psi$ can be taken clean: within each clause no literal is
repeated, and no two literals share the same underlying variable.
\end{theorem}

\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, dtDepth}
Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2)$ — more precisely $f$ a Boolean function on $n$
variables — have decision-tree depth at most $d$. Then $f$ is computed by a DNF formula
$\varphi$ (a disjunction of terms, each term a conjunction of literals) of width at most
$d$, meaning every term of $\varphi$ contains at most $d$ literals, such that
$\varphi(x) = f(x)$ for all inputs $x$. Moreover each term of $\varphi$ is tidy: no
literal is repeated within a term, and no two literals in the same term share a variable
(equivalently, within any one term each variable occurs at most once, and with a single
fixed polarity).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Functional switching lemma under Bernoulli restrictions]
\lean{LMN.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_function}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b001,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b003,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b004
}
\label{LMN.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_function}
\leanok
\uses{CNF.eval, LMN.dtDepth_congr, LMN.dtDepth_le_implies_nice_cnf, LMN.restrictFn_congr, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ whose
decision-tree depth is at most $w$, for some integer $w \ge 1$. Let $p$ be a real
parameter with $0 < p \le 1/(40w)$ (so in particular $p \le 1$), and draw a
Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables: independently, each
variable is left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each
with probability $(1-p)/2$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$, the restricted function
$f\restriction\rho$ (that is, $f$ evaluated on the free coordinates with the remaining
coordinates set by $\rho$) satisfies
\[
\bbP_\rho\big[\, \text{decision-tree depth of } f\restriction\rho > t \,\big] \;\le\;
\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\,\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[General two-stage restriction bound]
\lean{LMN.two_stage_bound}
\label{LMN.two_stage_bound}
\leanok
\uses{LMN.composeRestr, LMN.restriction_compose_eq, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb_le_one', SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg', SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_sum_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$, let $E$ and $A$ be events on restrictions of $n$ variables,
and let $\beta \ge 0$. Write $\Pr_p[\,\cdot\,]$ for the probability of an event under a
Bernoulli($p$) random restriction, and for restrictions $\rho_1, \rho_2$ let $\rho_1
\circ \rho_2$ denote their composition (the values fixed by $\rho_1$, filled in by
$\rho_2$ on the coordinates $\rho_1$ leaves free). Suppose that for every restriction
$\rho_1$ for which $A(\rho_1)$ fails, one has $\Pr_{p_2}[\,E(\rho_1 \circ \rho_2)\,] \le
\beta$. Then
\[
  \Pr_{p_1 p_2}[E] \;\le\; \Pr_{p_1}[A] + \beta .
\]
\end{theorem}

\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.compression_and_of_cnfs, LMN.exists_nice_cnf_of_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Fix natural numbers $n$, $s_2$, and $l$, a restriction $\rho_1$ on $n$ variables, and a
family of DNF formulas $g_0, g_1, \dots, g_{s_2-1}$ on $n$ variables. For each index
$i$, write $\tilde g_i$ for the restricted function $x \mapsto
g_i(\rho_1.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$, obtained by evaluating $g_i$ with the coordinates fixed
by $\rho_1$ set accordingly and the free coordinates supplied by $x$. Suppose that every
$\tilde g_i$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then there is a CNF formula $\Psi$ on
$n$ variables of width at most $l$ in which each clause has no repeated literal and no
two distinct literals sharing a variable, such that for every assignment $x$,
\[
\Psi(x) \;=\; \bigwedge_{i=0}^{s_2-1} \tilde g_i(x).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restricted conjunction of DNFs has a low-width simple CNF]
\lean{LMN.depth3_restricted_has_nice_cnf}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\label{LMN.depth3_restricted_has_nice_cnf}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.and_of_gates_has_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.extend, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_s$ be DNF formulas in $n$ Boolean variables, and let $f :
(\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be their conjunction, so that
$f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ if and only if $g_i(x) = \mathrm{true}$ for every $i$. Fix a
restriction $\rho$ of the $n$ variables, and write $h_\rho$ for the restriction of a
Boolean function $h$ by $\rho$ (the function obtained by fixing each coordinate that
$\rho$ sets and leaving the rest free). Suppose that for every $i$ the restricted gate
$(g_i)_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then the restricted function $f_\rho$
is computed by some CNF formula $\Psi$ of width at most $l$ — every clause contains at
most $l$ literals — in which each clause is simple: no literal occurs twice, and any two
literals in a clause that share a variable are identical. That is, $\Psi(x) = f_\rho(x)$
for all $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second-stage switching bound for an AND of DNFs]
\lean{LMN.depth3_second_stage_bound}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p014-b001
}
\label{LMN.depth3_second_stage_bound}
\leanok
\uses{CNF.eval, DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.cleanCNF_D3, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_eval, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_nodup, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_var_inj, LMN.cleanCNF_D3_width_le, LMN.composeRestr, LMN.depth3_restricted_has_nice_cnf, LMN.dtDepth_congr, LMN.restrictFn_composeRestr, LMN.restrictFn_congr, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables, and write
$D(h)$ for the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function $h$, i.e. the least depth of a
decision tree computing it. Suppose $f$ is the conjunction $f=g_1\wedge\cdots\wedge
g_{s_2}$ of DNF formulas $g_1,\dots,g_{s_2}$, meaning $f(x)=1$ exactly when $g_i(x)=1$
for every $i$. Fix a restriction $\rho_1$ on the $n$ variables such that each restricted
gate satisfies $D(g_i\!\restriction\!\rho_1)\le l$, where $l\ge 1$, and let $t$ be a
natural number. Suppose $0<p_2\le \tfrac{1}{40l}$ (so in particular $p_2\le 1$), and let
$\rho_2$ be a Bernoulli($p_2$) random restriction — each variable independently left
free with probability $p_2$ and fixed to $0$ or $1$ with probability $(1-p_2)/2$ each.
Writing $\rho_1\circ\rho_2$ for the composite restriction that applies $\rho_1$ first
and then $\rho_2$ on the coordinates left free by $\rho_1$, we have
\[
\Pr_{\rho_2}\!\big[\, D\big(f\!\restriction\!(\rho_1\circ\rho_2)\big) > t
\,\big]\;\le\;\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t}+\exp\!\big(-n\,p_2/3\big).
\]
\end{lemma}

  {pdf-fc447f326910-p014-b001,
    pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
    pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.depth3_second_stage_bound, LMN.switching_bernoulli_union_bound, LMN.two_stage_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n \ge 1$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be the conjunction of $s_2$ DNF
formulas $g_1, \dots, g_{s_2}$ on $n$ variables, so that $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ exactly
when $g_i(x) = \mathrm{true}$ for every $i$. Suppose each $g_i$ has width at most $w$,
where $w \ge 1$, and that within every term of every $g_i$ no literal is repeated and no
two distinct literals share the same variable. Fix natural numbers $l \ge 1$ and $t$,
together with real parameters $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$ satisfying $p_1 \le 1/(40w)$ and $p_2
\le 1/(40l)$. Writing $D(g)$ for the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function $g$ and
$f\restriction_\rho$ for the restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho\text{-extension of
}x)$, a Bernoulli$(p_1 p_2)$ random restriction $\rho$ then satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{\rho}\!\big[\, D(f\restriction_\rho) > t \,\big]
  \;\le\;
  s_2\Big( \big(\tfrac12\big)^{l} + \exp\!\big(-\tfrac{n p_1}{3}\big) \Big)
  \;+\;
  \Big( \big(\tfrac12\big)^{t} + \exp\!\big(-\tfrac{n p_2}{3}\big) \Big).
\]
\end{theorem}

  {LMN.depth3_switching_bound}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}
  {pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b003,
    pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.composedDelta, LMN.depth3_switching_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n \ge 1$, and let $f\colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be the conjunction of $s_2$ DNF
formulas $g_1,\dots,g_{s_2}$, so that $f(x)=1$ if and only if $g_i(x)=1$ for every $i$.
Assume a width bound $w \ge 1$ under which each $g_i$ has width at most $w$ (every term
of every gate has at most $w$ literals), and assume that within each term of each gate
the literals are distinct and no variable occurs twice. Fix integers $l \ge 1$ and $t$,
and let $\rho$ be a Bernoulli random restriction with parameter
$\frac{1}{40w}\cdot\frac{1}{40l}$; write $p_1=\frac{1}{40w}$ and $p_2=\frac{1}{40l}$.
Write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function obtained by extending each input with the
values $\rho$ fixes, and let $D(\cdot)$ denote decision-tree depth (the least depth of a
decision tree computing the given function). Then the probability that the restricted
function has decision-tree depth exceeding $t$ obeys
\[
\Pr_\rho\!\big[\,D(f\!\restriction_\rho) > t\,\big]
\;\le\; s_2\big((1/2)^{l} + e^{-n p_1/3}\big) + \big((1/2)^{t} + e^{-n p_2/3}\big).
\]
\end{lemma}

  {LMN.circuit_reduction_depth3}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}
  {pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b003}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.circuit_reduction_depth3, LMN.composedDelta, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ with $n\ge 1$, and suppose $f$ is the conjunction of $s_2$
DNF formulas $D_1,\dots,D_{s_2}$, so that $f(x)=1$ exactly when $D_i(x)=1$ for every
index $i$; equivalently, $f$ is computed by a depth-three AND-of-OR-of-AND circuit.
Assume each formula $D_i$ has width at most $w$ with $w\ge 1$, and that within every
term no literal is repeated and no variable occurs in two opposite polarities, so that a
term reads each variable at most once. Fix integers $l\ge 1$ and $t\ge 0$ and a real
number $\varepsilon$ satisfying $s_2\,(1/2)^{l}\le \varepsilon/2$ and
$(1/2)^{t}\le\varepsilon/2$, and put $p_1=1/(40w)$ and $p_2=1/(40l)$. Draw a Bernoulli
random restriction $\rho$ with parameter $p_1 p_2$, and write $f_\rho$ for the
restriction of $f$ by $\rho$. Then the probability that the decision-tree depth of
$f_\rho$ exceeds $t$ is at most
\[
\varepsilon+s_2\,e^{-np_1/3}+e^{-np_2/3}.
\]
\end{theorem}
